items.claim_premise_extract: **The arena.** The non-relativistic quantum framework of this category uses as its spacetime the affine time space of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]]: a quadruple $(V,\tau,g,A)$ consisting of a four-dimensional real vector space $V$, a surject
targeted_actual_use_passages: **The arena.** The non-relativistic quantum framework of this category uses as its spacetime the affine time space of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]]: a quadruple $(V,\tau,g,A)$ consisting of a four-dimensional real vector space $V$, a surjective linear map $\tau:V\to\mathbb R$ (the **absolute-time covector**), the three-dimensional kernel $K=\ker\tau$ (the **spatial displacement space**), a symmetric positive definite bilinear form $g:K\times K\to\mathbb R$ (the **spatial metric**), and an affine space $A$ modelled on $V$ whose elements are called **events**. When the framework speaks of "a particle at position $x$ at time $t$", of "the time interval between two events" or of "the distance between two simultaneous events", these are read in this structure.

**Absolute time and slices.** The absolute time of a displacement $w\in V$ is $\tau(w)$; two events $p,q\in A$ are **simultaneous** when $\tau(q-p)=0$, and simultaneity is an equivalence relation whose classes are the **simultaneous slices**. For a fixed adapted chart and its coordinates $(t,x)$ of [[lem-cm-adapted-coordinates-exist-and-are-unique]], the slices are the level sets of $t$ and the number $t(p)$ is the **time coordinate** of the event $p$. The pair of events of one slice carries the slice distance $d_{g}(p,q)=\sqrt{g(p-q,p-q)}$; no distance is defined between events of different slices by this structure.

**Smooth structure.** $A$ is read with the affine smooth structure determined by adapted coordinates: for a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, a curve $\gamma:I\to A$ is of class $C^{k}$ when its coordinate representation $s\mapsto(t(\gamma(s)),x(\gamma(s)))$ in one adapted chart is of class $C^{k}$; the transition law between adapted charts of [[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]] makes this reading independent of the chart. Regularity of curves, of potential functions and of apparatus descriptions of the framework is stated with respect to this smooth structure.

**Status.** These clauses define the spacetime objects of the model and their elementary readings. They are not a physical postulate that nature is such an arena and not a mathematical theorem; the corresponding adoption is made by the kinematics postulate of this page. No dynamics, force law, potential or matter model is fixed here, and no empirical measurement is recorded.

- The coordinate space of the Galilean transformations of [[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]] is a model of the coordinate form of this arena: an adapted chart identifies $A$ bijectively with $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}$, and the transition law between two such charts is one of those transformations, as recorded in [[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]].
- Nothing in this definition fixes units. The readings of the time coordinate in seconds, of spatial coordinates in metres and of slice distances in metres are fixed by the unit and quantity conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

targeted_actual_use_passages: **Inertial frames.** Fix the arena $(V,\tau,g,A)$ of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]]. An **inertial frame** of the framework is an adapted chart

of that arena in the sense of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]]: an event $o\in A$ (the **spatial and time origin** of the frame), a vector $u\in V$ with $\tau(u)=1$ (the frame's **time vector**), and an ordered $g$-orthonormal positively oriented basis $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$ of $K$ (the frame's **spatial triad**). The associated **frame coordinates** are the functions $(t,x):A\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}$ of [[lem-cm-adapted-coordinates-exist-and-are-unique]], defined by $p=o+t(p)u+\sum_{i}x_{i}(p)e_{i}$.

**Allowed changes of frame.** Let $F$ and $F'$ be two inertial frames with coordinates $(t,x)$ and $(t',x')$. The **change of frame** from $F$ to $F'$ is the bijection of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}$ that sends the $F$-coordinates of an event to its $F'$-coordinates. By clause 1 of [[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]] there are $b\in\mathbb R$, $a,v\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $R\in SO(3)$ ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]) with

**Conventions.** The spatial triad of every frame is positively oriented for the fixed orientation of $K$ used in the definition of adapted charts, so all frame changes have $R\in SO(3)$ rather than $R\in O(3)$ with negative determinant. The reading of the coordinates in seconds and metres, and the physical meaning of the parameters as measured quantities, are fixed by the unit conventions recorded on this page; no measured value of any parameter is asserted here.

- The distinction between chart and congruence matters for later claims: a change of frame changes the coordinate description of a state or of a trajectory but does not move the apparatus, and an accelerated congruence of observers is not a frame of the model.
- Two inertial frames related by a pure time shift, a pure spatial translation, a pure boost or a pure rotation are the elementary cases listed in [[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]], and a general frame change is the composite of these.
- **Every Galilean map is realized by a pair of frames.** Fix $F=(o,u,(e_i))$ and any $(b,a,v,R)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\times SO(3)$. Define $e'_j:=\sum_iR_{ji}e_i$, $u':=u-\sum_i(R^{\mathsf T}v)_ie_i$, and $o':=o-bu+\sum_i(R^{\mathsf T}(vb-a))_ie_i$. Then $\tau(u')=1$, and $(e'_1,e'_2,e'_3)$ is a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal basis of $K$ because its change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal with determinant $\det R=1$. Thus $F':=(o',u',(e'_j))$ is an inertial frame. Substitution into $p=o+t u+\sum_i x_i e_i=o'+t'u'+\sum_jx'_je'_j$ gives $t'=t+b$ and $x'=Rx+vt+a$. Hence every parameter quadruple in the definition of $G$ occurs as the coordinate change of two inertial frames; combined with the adapted-chart lemma's forward direction, the class of changes is exactly $G$.

targeted_actual_use_passages:
- **Why the model is fixed through the scaling theorem.** The operator $H_1$ is not introduced as "the differential expression with some self-adjoint extension": it is the unique self-adjoint extension of the symmetric operator on the polynomial-Gaussian core that is fixed outright by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]]. The weak identity of clause (c) then records that this operator is the realization of the quadratic expression in the sense of distributions, without claiming that its domain coincides with any maximally defined differential domain.
- **The two realizations are separate adoptions.** Clause (b) declares a particle confined to a line; P5's spacetime arena is $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}$, so the one-dimensional model is an additional idealization, not a restriction of P5. Clause (d) is the isotropic three-dimensional model of P5 at $s=0$. Later items of this page state their hypotheses for one or the other realization explicitly; results about the one-dimensional realization are not transferred to the three-dimensional one or conversely, except where the multidimensional theorem supplies the identification.
- **Units.** The quantities $\ell$, $Q$, $P$, $H_1$, $H_3$, $m$, $\omega$ and $\hbar$ are read as dimensioned model quantities: $[\ell]=\ell$, $[Q]=\ell$, $[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$, $[H]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, $[m]=\mu$, $[\omega]=\tau^{-1}$ and $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$. The excitation number $N_\psi$ is dimensionless and is read in the declared unit $1/\mathrm{count}$; $V(0)$ is subtracted only as a potential-energy offset, and the quantum energy eigenvalues $\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$ are read in joules.

items.claim_premise_extract: Fix the spacetime arena of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]] together with an inertial frame $F$ of [[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]] with coordinates $(t,x)$. Every smooth chart of the arena of the form $$G_{w}:\mathbb R\time
targeted_actual_use_passages:
Fix the spacetime arena of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]] together with an inertial frame $F$ of [[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]] with coordinates $(t,x)$. Every smooth chart of the arena of the form
$$G_{w}:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3},\qquad G_{w}(t,x)=\bigl(t,\,x+w(t)\bigr),$$
with $w:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of class $C^{\infty}$ and $[w_i]=\ell$ for every component, is an inertial frame of the model; that is, the map $G_{w}$ belongs to the Galilean transformation class $G$ of [[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]] for every such $w$.

**Given:** The Galilean transformations $g_{(b,a,v,R)}(t,x)=(t+b,Rx+vt+a)$ and their parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]); the inertial frames of the arena, whose changes are exactly the Galilean transformations ([[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]], [[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]] clause 1); a nonzero vector $c\in\mathbb R^3$ with $[c_i]=\ell\tau^{-2}$; a velocity vector $u\in\mathbb R^3$ with $[u_i]=\ell\tau^{-1}$; a positive time scale $T_0$ with $[T_0]=\tau$; and the shear map $G(t,x):=(t,\,x+t^{2}c)$.

[L3] Coordinate velocities and accelerations of parametrized curves are the componentwise derivatives of the coordinate curves, and the second coordinate of the standard chart of the arena is identified with $x$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]]).

1.3 [A zero-acceleration curve becomes accelerating] Let $\gamma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}$ be $\gamma(s):=(s,us)$, where $s$ is a time coordinate. In the standard chart its coordinate curve is $x(s)=us$ with $x''=0$; in the chart $G$ it is $x'(s)=us+s^{2}c$, whose second derivative is $2c\ne0$. The terms $us$ and $s^2c$ both have dimension $\ell$, and their first and second derivatives have dimensions $\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $\ell\tau^{-2}$. Hence zero coordinate acceleration is not preserved by this chart, although it is preserved by every Galilean change of frame by clause 1 of [[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]]. targeted_actual_use_passages:
1. P1, the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]: nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces, unit rays and density operators as preparations, statistical mixtures, and composition by the completed tensor product.
2. P2, the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]: sharp observables as self-adjoint operators with declared units, their spectral probability measures, finite-resolution bins, and finite unsharp outcome families.
3. P3, the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]: the declared projective Lueders measurement, its outcome probabilities, its conditional update and its discarded-outcome ensemble.

Radiation and external-field models appear only through the explicitly adopted extensions above, never as a limit of the massive model of P5.

items.claim_premise_extract: Adopt as physical assumptions of the non-relativistic classical mechanics framework the following statements about spacetime. **(i) Spacetime data.** Spacetime is the mathematical structure $(V,\tau,g,A,\text{fixed orientation of }K)$ of [[
targeted_actual_use_passages: Adopt as physical assumptions of the non-relativistic classical mechanics framework the following statements about spacetime.

**(i) Spacetime data.** Spacetime is the mathematical structure
$(V,\tau,g,A,\text{fixed orientation of }K)$ of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]]: a
four-dimensional real vector space $V$; a surjective linear map
$\tau:V\to\mathbb R$, the **absolute-time covector**; the kernel
$K=\ker\tau$, a three-dimensional real vector space, the **spatial displacement
space**; a **spatial metric** $g$, a symmetric positive-definite bilinear form
$g:K\times K\to\mathbb R$; a fixed **orientation** of $K$, that is, a chosen one
of the two classes of ordered bases of $K$ under the equivalence generated by
positive-determinant changes of basis; and an affine space $A$ modelled on $V$
(a nonempty set with a free and transitive $V$-action, with displacements as in
[[def-cm-affine-time-space]]). The elements of $A$ are the **events** of the
model. The structure is the arena of the model; no equation of motion, force
law or matter content is asserted by this clause.

**(iii) Absolute time, simultaneity and distance.** Two events $p,q\in A$ are
**simultaneous** when their displacement lies in $K$, that is, when
$\tau(q-p)=0$. Simultaneity is an equivalence relation on $A$: it is reflexive
because $\tau(0)=0$, symmetric because $\tau(p-q)=-\tau(q-p)$ and transitive
because $\tau$ is additive. Its classes are the **simultaneous slices**
$A_{t}=\{p\in A:\tau(p-o)=t\}$ of any adapted chart; the class does not depend
on the choice of adapted chart, and the elapsed time between two events is the
chart-independent number $\tau(q-p)$. Two events of a common slice carry the
**slice distance** $d_{g}(p,q):=\sqrt{g(p-q,p-q)}$, which is defined because
$p-q\in K$; distances are not defined across distinct slices by this structure.

**(iv) Smooth structure.** $A$ is read with the affine smooth structure
determined by its affine coordinates: an adapted chart of
[[def-cm-affine-time-space]] is a bijection $A\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}$
whose inverse is the map $(t,x)\mapsto o+tu+\sum_{i}x_{i}e_{i}$, and curves are
declared $C^{k}$ when their coordinate functions in one (equivalently, every)
adapted chart are $C^{k}$. The equivalence of the two readings is supplied by
the affine transition law between adapted charts proved in
[[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]]; this postulate adopts
the resulting smooth structure as the one in which regularity of worldlines and
of force maps is stated.

**(ii) Description in another frame.** The same motion described in a second
inertial frame is the curve obtained by the time reparametrization of the two
frames: if $(t',x')$ are the coordinates of the second frame and
$t'=t+b$ is the time component of the transformation between the two frames
([[post-cm01-frames]], [[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]]),

$\gamma_{i,b}(t'):=\gamma_{i}(t'-b)$, defined on $I+b$, and it again satisfies

curve is twice continuously differentiable in one inertial frame exactly when
its reparametrized description is twice continuously differentiable in the
other. The assumptions of this postulate are therefore read in any one inertial
frame without loss.

  [[post-cm01-spacetime]]; particles moving at speeds small compared with the

  numerical cutoff and records no measurement.

targeted_actual_use_passages:
A rejection is a decision about the specified triple of null family,
apparatus behaviour and sampling assumptions. It is evidence against that
triple at the declared size; it is not a proof that a force law, a spacetime,
or classical mechanics is false, and the realized discrepancy does not by
itself identify which ingredient failed. A discrepancy may expose the force
law, a wrong or incomplete calibration, a changed preparation, correlated
errors violating the sampling hypothesis, or an analysis error; separating
these requires further stated models and further data. Conversely, retaining
the null is not proof of the null: a test with low power fails to reject
alternatives it cannot distinguish, and nonrejection alone neither proves nor estimates an effect size. Under a specified family the nonrejection event has parameter-dependent probability $1-\beta(\theta)$ and can therefore inform comparisons of effect values; quantification requires that family and an explicit inferential construction.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following **rigid-material
model** branch, in the spacetime and frames of [[post-cm01-spacetime]] and
[[post-cm01-frames]].

**(ii) Time window and motions.** A model carries a **time window**
$I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$, a nondegenerate open interval $(a,b)$ with
$-\infty\le a<b\le+\infty$ and at least two points, read in seconds. Fix an
**inertial frame** of the model, that is the adapted chart
$(o,u,(e_1,e_2,e_3))$ with coordinates $(t,x)$ of [[post-cm01-frames]]. A
**motion** of the model in this frame is a map
$x:I_0\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ for which there exist a map
$c:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ and a map $R:I_0\to SO(3)$, both of class $C^2$
(componentwise derivatives, [[def-cm-affine-time-space]] for the coordinates
and [[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]] for the target), such that
$$x(t,\rho)=c(t)+R(t)\rho\qquad(t\in I_0,\ \rho\in\mathbb R^3).$$
Adopt: the motions of the model are the maps of this form, and the pair
$(c,R)$ is the **configuration path** of the motion. The map
$x(t,\cdot):\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ is the **placement** at time $t$ and is
the rigid placement of [[def-cm-rigid-placement-and-body-angular-velocity]]
with translation $c$ and rotation $R$; its material velocity is
$\partial_tx(t,\rho)=c'(t)+R'(t)\rho$, defined by differentiability of $c$ and
of the entries of $R$. The time window $I_0$ is the interval on which the
model's configuration path is considered; the model's time coordinate is
the frame time $t$.

**(d) Description in another inertial frame.** Let a second inertial frame be
related to the first by the transformation $t'=t+b$, $x'=Qx+ut+a$ of
[[post-cm01-frames]] clause (iv), with $b\in\mathbb R$, $a,u\in\mathbb R^3$
and $Q\in SO(3)$
([[lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations]] clause 1); the letters
$Q$ and $u$ are the rotation and the boost velocity written $R$ and $v$ in
[[post-cm01-frames]], renamed to avoid clashes with the orientation path
$R(t)$ and the material velocity field of clause (e). The
**description of the same motion in the second frame** assigns to the same
material label $\rho$ the events of the motion in the new coordinates,
$$\tilde x(t',\rho):=Q\,x(t'-b,\rho)+u\,(t'-b)+a .$$
Substituting $x(t,\rho)=c(t)+R(t)\rho$ and using distributivity of the matrix
product over sums expresses the description as a motion of the same model in
the second frame, with configuration path
$$\tilde c(t')=Qc(t'-b)+u\,(t'-b)+a,\qquad \tilde R(t')=Q\,R(t'-b),$$
where $\tilde R(t')\in SO(3)$ for every $t'$ because $SO(3)$ is closed under
matrix multiplication ([[lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group]]); the pair
$(\tilde c,\tilde R)$ is again of class $C^2$. This description is a
convention forced by the frame change,
not a dynamical statement; the transformation laws of the velocity field, the
angular velocity and the inertia data are proved in the frame-covariance
theorem of this page.

targeted_actual_use_passages:
**(b) Coordinate curves, velocities and accelerations.** Let $J\subseteq I$
be an interval with nonempty interior and let $x:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a
curve of class $C^{2}$ in the inertial chart (for instance the coordinate
curve of a worldline in the sense of [[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]). The
**coordinate curve of $x$ in the moving chart** is
$$y(t):=R(t)^{\mathsf T}\bigl(x(t)-c(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J);$$
its **coordinate velocity** and **coordinate acceleration in the moving
chart** are the componentwise derivatives $\dot y:=y'$ and $\ddot y:=y''$
([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), of dimensions
$\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $\ell\tau^{-2}$. These are chart-local notions: because
the chart is generally time-dependent, these need not be the coordinate
velocity and acceleration of an inertial frame. If $R$ is constant and $c$ is
affine on $I$, they agree on $I$ with the corresponding quantities in the
inertial frame whose adapted chart restricts to this chart. Their relation to
the fixed frame $F$ is the kinematic identity of the cited mathematical
supplier, not an identification with the quantities read in $F$.

**(e) Curves at rest in the chart.** For fixed $y_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ let
$x_{y_{0}}(s):=R(s)y_{0}+c(s)$ be the spatial coordinate curve in the inertial
chart. Its spacetime lift is the curve $\gamma_{y_{0}}:I\to A$ defined by
$$\gamma_{y_{0}}(s):=o+su+\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(x_{y_{0}}(s)\bigr)_{j}e_{j}.$$
It is $C^{2}$ and satisfies $t(\gamma_{y_{0}}(s))=s$, so it has the
parameter condition of [[post-cm01-worldlines]]. This lifted curve is the path
of a point **at rest in the chart**; whether it is assigned as the worldline of
a particle label is a separate declaration of a model and is not made here.

**(f) Status.** A moving chart is a time-dependent coordinate description
attached to one inertial frame. In general it is not an inertial frame of the
model: [[post-cm01-frames]] defines inertial charts using a fixed spatial basis
and an affine reference curve. When $R$ is constant and $c$ is affine on $I$,
the coordinate change has the form of an allowed Galilean frame change and is
the restriction to $I$ of an adapted chart. The inertial-forces theorem of
this page proves that these are exactly the data for which the inertial terms
of clause (d) vanish identically. A moving chart is not an observer
congruence: a congruence is a family of curves of the spacetime data, whereas
a chart is a coordinate map. The identity
relating the inertial-chart acceleration to the moving-chart acceleration of
the same curve is the mathematical lemma cited in clause (c); the equation of
motion of a force model in the moving chart, with the inertial terms entering
as the mass multiples $m\tau$, is the inertial-forces theorem of this page,
with its own hypotheses. Nothing in this definition asserts a force law, an
equation of motion, a transformation law for physical interactions or a
measured value.
